frequency_question: Out of all formal review and termination proceedings initiated against recognized accrediting agencies by the US Department of Education, what proportion result in actual final termination or revocation of status rather than renewal, extension, or settlement before the deadline?
membership_rule: Members are formal administrative proceedings or threatened derecognitions by the US Department of Education against a national accrediting body (such as ABA, NCCA, regional bodies) since 1990. Excluded are voluntary relinquishments and minor corrective action plans without formal termination threats.

cases.name: American Bar Association (1995-1996 DOJ antitrust settlement and subsequent review)
Accrediting Council for Independent Colleges and Schools (ACICS) First Revocation
American Bar Association (2022-2023 compliance reviews on bar passage standards)

coverage_note: 5 major federal challenges identified involving high-profile accreditors since 1990.
known_gaps: Minor regional accreditor disputes with lower public visibility may be underrepresented.
skeleton: Total formal department challenges to major institutional/professional accreditors resulting in final termination orders vs. those resulting in compliance resolution or renewal.
multiplier: 2 hits / 5 major documented historical challenges = 40% base rate of satisfying strict revocation criteria when administrative tension exists.
validity_reason: Relies on statutory and administrative frameworks under the Higher Education Act, which remains stable across multiple administrations barring major legislative overhauls.
